previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy (EF 20%), ischemic heart disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and GERD, was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and visual hallucinations. He presented with signs of heart failure exacerbation, including orthopnea, bilateral leg edema, and pulmonary edema on imaging, with a markedly elevated BNP of 6797. He was treated with IV furosemide and transitioned to oral torsemide, resulting in improved symptoms and a weight reduction from 139.2kg to 136.3kg. The visual hallucinations, occurring upon waking and recognized as unreal, were attributed to poor sleep and resolved during admission. His mild troponin elevation was deemed consistent with demand ischemia. Medications were optimized, including increasing omeprazole for GERD. He was discharged home with clear instructions on diuretic use, daily weight monitoring, and follow-up with cardiology.
